chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from al-'Abbas ibn 'Amir, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from the one who narrated to him, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) granted permission for cutting the two branches of the Mahalah, which is the Bakarah that is drawn from the trees of the Haram and the Idhkhir.
And it has been narrated that whoever pulls up a tree from the Haram, its expiation is a cow, whose meat he gives in charity to the poor. He narrated.

key_terms.الْإِذْخِر: A type of fragrant shrub or tree found in the Hijaz
key_terms.الْبَكَرَة: A young tree or branch, specifically one used for drawing water or identified in this context
key_terms.الْحَرَم: The sacred precincts, specifically referring to the holy sites where specific rules apply
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَة: Expiation or compensation for a violation
key_terms.الْمَحَالَة: A specific type of branch or shoot from sacred trees

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for uprooting a tree in the Haram according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific botanical exemptions (Mahalah and Bakarah) within the Haram's sacred groves, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Prophet and Imam al-Sadiq regarding resource management in the holy precincts. It complements the general rule of expiation for uprooting trees by detailing the precise nature of the permitted cuttings, highlighting the distinction between minor harvesting and total removal. The mention of the cow as expiation underscores the continuity of pre-Islamic and early Islamic sacrificial customs within Shia legal tradition.
